methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Myanmar Earthquakes: Damage Proxy Maps, Interferograms and Pixel Offset Maps, Mar 2025

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage proxy maps, interferograms and pixel offset maps for Myanmar Earthquakes (Mar 2025) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Naypyidaw Vicinity, Myanmar, Earthquakes, 05 Apr 2025, v0.9** (superseded)
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Myanmar, Earthquakes, 5 Apr 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Myanmar, Earthquakes, 3 Apr 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Myanmar, Earthquakes, 3 Apr 2025, v0.5** (superseded)
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Naypyidaw Vicinity, Myanmar, Earthquakes, 31 Mar 2025, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Pixel Offset Map (Sentinel-2 Data): Myanmar, Earthquakes, Pre-Event: 2025/03/25-27 NORTHING**
- **EOS-RS Interferogram (Unwrapped): Myanmar, Earthquakes, 2025/02/16-2025/03/30, v0.1**
- **EOS-RS Interferogram (Wrapped): Myanmar, Earthquakes, 2025/02/16-2025/03/30, v0.1**

organization.title: Earth Observatory of Singapore
organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Naypyidaw Vicinity, Myanmar, Earthquakes, 05 Apr 2025, v0.9

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

Superseded by a later version in this dataset.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas that are likely damaged in the vicinity of Naypyidaw, Myanmar, due to the Mw7.7 earthquake on 28 Mar 2025 and its aftershocks until 5 Apr 2025. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (27 Jul 2024 to 24 Mar 2025) and after (05 Apr 2025) the event.

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary pixel offset map to assess two-dimensional displacements in the northing direction along the Sagaing Fault in Myanmar after the Mw7.7 earthquake on 28 Mar 2025 and its aftershocks until 1 Apr 2025. This map was derived from optical images acquired by the Sentinel-2 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (25 Mar & 27 Mar 2025) and after (30 Mar & 1 Apr 2025) the event.
